links.outcome: Segmentation performance change after vendor software version upgrade
links.effect: After upgrade from RayStation 12A to 2024B, humerus outliers increased and 4 trend shifts occurred (none under 12A), moving average shifted outside control limits; heart outliers decreased
links.quote: For RayStation version 12A, no trend shifts were reported for the humerus, whereas 4 trend shifts were reported for version 2024B.

openai.sample_unit: regions of interest with paired deep-learning and clinically approved segmentations
models_evaluated: Embedded deep learning segmentation model in RayStation versions 12A and 2024B
In-house deep learning segmentation model trained by Bakx et al.

links.outcome: Automatic detection of clinically significant segmentation performance deterioration
links.effect: Continuous monitoring detected a clinically significant humerus performance drop, reflected in 4 trend shifts after the software upgrade. Sensitivity and specificity were not tested.
links.quote: Although the current setup was not tested for sensitivity and specificity, with the integration of the CQA framework, a clinically significant performance drop of the humerus was detected automatically.

links.outcome: Automatic outlier detection using statistical control limits and adapted Nelson rules
links.effect: Rules flagged 88 outliers with larger adjustments and 5 with fewer adjustments, representing 3.0 % of ROIs. Flagged cases underwent manual investigation.
links.quote: Rule 1 detected 88 outliers with larger adjustments and 5 with less adjustments.

links.outcome: Identification of errors through segmentation comparison and manual investigation
links.effect: Comparison of AI segmentations with clinically approved delineations flagged 93 outliers; manual investigation identified 12 human errors.
links.quote: These 93 outliers were manually investigated and from them 12 were found to be human errors.

links.outcome: Local segmentation performance deterioration following treatment-planning software upgrade
links.effect: Humerus trend shifts increased from none with RayStation version 12A to 4 with version 2024B; the moving average shifted outside the control limits.
links.quote: For RayStation version 12A, no trend shifts were reported for the humerus, whereas 4 trend shifts were reported for version 2024B.

links.effect: The monitoring framework successfully used statistical process control to automatically report outliers and trend shifts in real-time use.
links.quote: A CQA framework for DLS was successfully implemented using SPC and adapted Nelson rules to automatically report outliers and trend shifts, which led to automatic detection of such deviations.

links.effect: Logging edit rates showed that clinicians made consistently fewer adjustments to AI segmentations during live clinical practice compared to commissioning.
links.quote: Although not statistically significant, the difference in Table 3 showed that consistently less adjustments were made to the DLS in clinical practice than during commissioning.

links.effect: Predefined statistical thresholds automatically identified 93 outliers, and subsequent manual investigation found 12 human errors.
links.quote: These 93 outliers were manually investigated and from them 12 were found to be human errors.

links.effect: After upgrading to a new software version, four trend shifts indicating a performance drop were reported for humerus segmentations.
links.quote: For RayStation version 12A, no trend shifts were reported for the humerus, whereas 4 trend shifts were reported for version 2024B.
